speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you're experiencing fatigue, difficulty concentrating, and abnormal blood findings. To begin our assessment, how would you describe the onset and duration of these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient has a 3-week history of fatigue, difficulty to concentrate, and dyspnea on exertion. He also experiences dizziness and digital pain that improves with cold. He has a long history of smoking.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Your symptoms of fatigue, dizziness, and "pain that improves with cold" are quite specific. Given your history of smoking, could you describe the character of your chest pain or shortness of breath, and have you noticed any changes in your skin color or nail beds?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fatigue and difficulty to concentrate. I also have Dyspnea on exertion, Dizziness, Digital pain that improves with cold.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Raynaud's phenomenon secondary to Systemic Sclerosis (Scleroderma). The combination of fatigue, dyspnea, and digital pain that improves with cold (paradoxical response to warming, though the patient may perceive it as relief from the burning sensation of cold) is highly suggestive of an underlying autoimmune vasculopathy. Given the smoking history, we must rule out lung involvement, but the specific digital symptom pattern points strongly to scleroderma.

REQUEST TEST: ANA, ENA panel, ESR, CRP, Pulmonary_Function_Tests.
REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CT, Hand_Photos.
